Tested, nice.
Fix the sentence after XOR, there are line returns, it should be : "Two bits produce 1 if they are different, otherwise 0."

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: Clear instructions, fun puzzle that you need to use functions you dont usually touch, surprisingly short and simple solution once you get it.

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: J'accepte cette contribution parce que le message st claire est donne un indice sans dévoiler la solution.
You can use the fonction bin(numbre) in Python.

Goal
* Please remove all monospace formatting.

* Please format all numbers as {{constants}}.

* Please format "N" as a [[variable]].

Constraints
* Please change 1000000000 to 10⁹.

Cases
* Validator 3: Please change the input to 682, so that the case is similar to Test 3.

* Validator 4: Please change the input to 511, so that the case is similar to Test 4.

* Please add these cases with the specified inputs:
  Test 5: 51657
  Validator 5: 39321
  Test 6: 6053991
  Validator 6: 4299818
  Test 7: 283233306
  Validator 7: 528130328
  Test 8: 1000000000
  Validator 8: 999999999

Thanks.

Thanks a lot for the detailed review! I've updated the formatting, fixed the XOR description, adjusted the validators and added all the requested test cases. Really appreciate the feedback and the time you took to review the puzzle!
Thanks for testing it and catching that! I've fixed the formatting so the XOR explanation appears on a single line. Appreciate the feedback!
Sorry I can't approve, I haven't played enough clashes of code :-(

Thank you for your update.

Goal
* Please format "N" in the example as a [[variable]].

Constraints
* For consistency, please either format 10⁹ as a constant, or remove the formatting from 1.

Cases
* Just to clarify the new cases I suggested in my previous comment: they're intended to improve test coverage (e.g. by including different scenarios where the output can be 0), as well as to cover the range of possible input values in a more balanced and even manner.

Thanks again.

Thanks again! I've fixed the variable and constant formatting as requested. Also, I understand your point about the additional test cases and improving the coverage across different inputs and outputs. Really appreciate you taking the time to help improve the puzzle!

If everything looks good now, would you mind approving the contribution? I'd really appreciate it! And of course, if there's anything else you think could be improved, I'm happy to make further adjustments.

I think it would be good to give others a chance to review the contribution as well, just in case I might have missed something. I appreciate your work on this and your willingness to make further adjustments!
